subject: Post-call: latency constraints & hosted vs current provider
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@systrace.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: latency constraints & hosted vs current provider

Thanks again for your time today — quick written recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call summary (high level):
- You described a customer-facing inference path for document summarization + search re-ranking.
- Current vendor numbers you shared: end-to-end p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 2.5s under production traffic spikes (bursts up to 75 qps).
- Streaming is used for long-generation responses; many callers use streaming+partial-rendering to improve perceived latency.

Our initial qualification notes:
- Redwood hosted target we suggested on the call: end-to-end p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 600 ms for the typical 512-token gen path (batching disabled at low concurrency). These are achievable with our optimized runtime but we need to validate on your exact workload.
- Key variables we need from you to scope a fair test: steady QPS / burst patterns, average & 95th token lengths, percent of streaming calls, and a sample request set.

Proposed next steps:
1) You provide sample workload (requests + headers) and a representative traffic profile (CSV).
2) We run two scoped tests: (A) short-window hosted benchmark (2 x 30-minute runs) against our hosted API with production routing, (B) a side-by-side run (if you can provide current-vendor logs / traces) to compare p95/p99 under identical load.
3) Confirm streaming behavior we should replicate (chunk sizes, SSE vs chunked, client timeouts).

Attachments: redwood-slo-test-plan.xlsx (test cases + measurement rubric).

Immediate asks for you: please drop the sample workload and tell us the preferred 48-hour window for the test. If sharing logs is sensitive, a sanitized sample trace is fine.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate engineers once we lock the window.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@systrace.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@bankcorp.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency constraints & hosted vs current provider

Thanks Mina — great summary. Quick answers and a sample payload attached.

Our targets:
- Business target: p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 900 ms end-to-end (including network + client rendering) for the 90% of calls that are 256 tokens or shorter. Anything better is a win.
- Hard constraint: p99 must not exceed 1.5s for SLAs in EU banking pilot.

Current production profile (high level):
- Steady-state: 20 qps average.
- Burst/peak: up to 80 qps for ~10-minute windows (every 3 hours).
- Concurrency (per-host): normally 8–16 concurrent open requests.
- Streaming: ~35% of requests use streaming. They prefer SSE with ~200-token chunking.

I attached systrace-workload-sample.json — it's ~2000 requests drawn from production (sanitized). We cannot share unredacted vendor logs yet; legal needs NDA (linked separately).

Preferred test window: Jul 6–8 (PST) — we can make test environment mirrors available.

Oliver
Head of Platform, Systrace AI
oliver@systrace.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@systrace.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-01T18:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency constraints & hosted vs current provider

Perfect — got the sample workload, thanks. A few clarifications so our test matrix is tight:

Questions / clarifications:
- When you say p95/p99 end-to-end: do you include client rendering time? For apples-to-apples, we plan to measure server-to-server E2E (front door -> model -> payload delivered). We can add a client-side measurement if you prefer.
- For streaming: we will emulate SSE with 200-token chunks. Can you confirm typical chunk interval (e.g., 150–400ms per chunk)?
- TLS termination: will the test environment mirror your production TLS profile (mutual TLS or standard TLS)?

Proposed test matrix (summary):
- Test A (baseline): 20 qps steady, single-worker concurrency settings to match your production host (8–16).
- Test B (burst): ramp to 80 qps for 10 minutes, measure p50/p95/p99 and observed tail behavior.
- Test C (streaming): 35% streaming mix with 200-token chunks at 300ms average chunk interval (we’ll tune if you specify otherwise).

We will run each test twice (morning/evening) and attach full histograms and flamegraphs. Expected deliverables: CSVs of response times, per-route token counts, and a short runbook describing where tail latency came from (queueing vs model decode).

For the NDA: the DocuSign link in the related_links list should work; sign that and we’ll share deeper traces.

I attached redwood-test-instructions.md with the exact curl commands and header sets we’ll use. Please confirm the chunk interval and your preferred test window (Jul 6–8 is fine on our side).

—
Mina
